task: Oracle dialect: support the optional `WHERE` clause on the `UPDATE` and `INSERT` branches of a `MERGE` statement (`WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ... WHERE ...`, `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT ... VALUES ... WHERE ...`), so it parses and round-trips in Oracle. When transpiling to dialects that do not support it, emit an unsupported warning and drop the clause.
why:
Fidelity decided it. c1 stores the branch condition as a proper `exp.Where` on a new optional `When.where` argument, parses it with the existing `_parse_where`, and prints it with the existing `where_sql`.
c2 instead puts a bare condition (not wrapped in `exp.Where`) into `Update.where` / `Insert.where`. Everywhere else in the code base those arguments hold a `Where` node. So the tree has an unusual shape, and rendering that `Update` on its own would lose the `WHERE` keyword. Only c2's custom handling inside `when_sql` covers this.
Both patches have the same scope: they parse and round-trip the clause for Oracle and warn and drop it for other dialects. Both pass all tests. c2 also adds extra test imports (`ErrorLevel`, `helper_logger`) and an explicit `unsupported_level` argument that c1's test does without.
